intro: A couple of little apps I built for myself while learning Japanese, shared here as extra resources. They're homemade developer builds — not polished store releases — but they work.

apps.name: YappyJappy
apps.tagline: A chat partner for practicing Japanese — furigana over every kanji, gentle corrections, and readings the moment you need them.
apps.summary: YappyJappy is a chat app for practicing everyday Japanese. You talk back and forth with an AI conversation partner that writes at your level, sets furigana over every kanji, quietly fixes the mistakes in what you just said, and glosses the words it thinks are new to you. Save any word or sentence to your vocab list and keep the conversation going.
howItWorks: It started as a fix for one specific frustration. Having a practice conversation with a plain AI chatbot means the replies come back in kanji you might not be able to read yet — and when you ask for the readings, everything turns into a wall of hiragana that's just as hard to parse. There was never a clean way to see a kanji and its reading together, the way a Japanese book prints them.

So YappyJappy formats every reply for a learner. After each word that contains kanji, the reading is shown as small furigana sitting right above the characters — real ruby text — so you can read naturally and only glance up when you need to.

When your last message had a mistake, the reply opens with a ✏️ line showing the corrected sentence and a short note on what changed, then carries on chatting like normal. If you didn't slip up, it just keeps the conversation going. Words it guesses are above your level get a quick English gloss in parentheses, and every reply ends with a plain-English translation for when you get stuck.

Anything worth keeping — a single word or a whole sentence, with its reading and meaning — saves to a vocab list in one tap. Your conversations stay on the device, so you can pick any of them back up later.

features.title: Furigana over every kanji
features.body: Readings sit above the characters as ruby text, so you can read at a glance and check yourself only when you need to.

features.title: Fixes mistakes as you go
features.body: A ✏️ correction line shows what you should have said, and a short note on why — without breaking the flow of the chat.

features.title: Explains the hard words
features.body: English glosses on vocabulary above your level, plus a full plain-English translation of every reply.

features.title: Save words & sentences
features.body: Build a personal vocab list with readings and meanings, one tap at a time.

features.title: Reads it out loud
features.body: Built-in text-to-speech speaks the Japanese so you can hear how it sounds.

features.title: Your choice of AI
features.body: Works with Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI), or Gemini (Google) using your own API key — pick the provider and model you like.

features.title: Tune the conversation
features.body: A prompt library keeps different setups — beginner chat, JLPT drills, keigo practice — so you can switch with a tap.

features.title: Backup & restore
features.body: Export your conversations, vocab, and prompts to a file, and bring them back any time.

requirements: An API key from Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google — you bring your own, and the app talks straight to that provider
install: Download the APK below onto your Android phone.

Open the downloaded file. Android will ask whether to allow installs from your browser or Files app — allow it. This is the normal "install unknown apps" prompt for anything that doesn't come from the Play Store.
In the app's Settings, choose your provider (Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini), paste your API key, and pick a model.
Start a new chat and say hi. It'll ask what you'd like to talk about or practice.
apps.privacy: YappyJappy talks straight to whichever AI provider you choose, using the API key you enter — nothing is routed through this site or any server of mine. Your conversations and saved vocab live on your phone.
apps.buildNote: This is a developer (debug) build, shared as-is — the same app I use day to day, not a Play Store release. It installs by sideloading, which is why Android shows the extra permission prompt.

apps.name: TapLex
apps.tagline: Draw a box over any on-screen text — a game, a manga panel, a menu — and tap the words to get readings, meanings, and a pop-up dictionary right where you're reading.
apps.summary: TapLex is a floating overlay that turns text in any app into a tappable dictionary. Point it at a region of the screen — a line of game dialogue, a manga panel, a menu — and it captures just that box, hands the crop to the AI you picked, and lays the sentence back out as clickable words with furigana over the kanji. Tap a word for its reading, meaning, and part of speech; ask a follow-up when you want more. Save anything worth keeping to a word list, and every capture is kept in your history.
howItWorks: It solves a specific kind of stuck. When you're reading Japanese in a game or a manga, the text is baked into the image — you can't select it, so you can't look anything up. Switching to a dictionary or an OCR app means leaving the thing you're reading, retyping what you can make out, and losing your place.

TapLex floats a little bubble over everything instead. Tap it and drag a box over the text you're stuck on. It hides itself so it won't show up in the shot, snaps a screenshot of just that region, then hands the crop to whichever AI you've set up.

A moment later the same box fills with the sentence rebuilt as tappable words, with the reading printed as small furigana above each kanji. Tap any word and a popup gives its reading, meaning, and part of speech, plus a short note on nuance and a button to hear it spoken.

Still not sure why a word means what it does? Ask a follow-up right in the popup and it explains, in the context of that sentence. Save any word to your list in a tap, flip the box between the translation and the game underneath so you never lose your place, and revisit anything later from your history.

features.title: Draw a box over anything
features.body: The overlay rides over any app — games, manga readers, browsers, menus. Position a box over the exact text you're stuck on and capture just that.

features.title: Tappable words with furigana
features.body: The captured sentence comes back as clickable chips, with the reading set above every kanji as ruby text.

features.title: Pop-up dictionary
features.body: Tap a word for its reading, meaning, part of speech, and a one-line note on nuance — without ever leaving the game.

features.title: Ask a follow-up
features.body: Chat back for a deeper explanation of a word or grammar point, answered in the context of the sentence you're reading.

features.title: Hear it out loud
features.body: Built-in text-to-speech speaks the word, with optional higher-quality Azure neural voices if you add a key.

features.title: Save words & keep history
features.body: Build a categorized word list one tap at a time, and every capture is stored so you can go back to it.

features.title: Your choice of AI
features.body: Works with Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI), or Gemini (Google) using your own API key — pick the provider and model you like.

features.title: Toggle between views
features.body: Flip a box between the translated words and the game showing through underneath, so you can check the original at a glance.

features.title: Reads many languages
features.body: Not just Japanese — pick the language you're reading and the one you want back, with runtime switching across 14 languages.

requirements: Permission to draw over other apps, plus a screen-capture permission — the app asks for both on first run so it can show the box and snapshot the text inside it
An API key from Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google — you bring your own, and the app talks straight to that provider
install: Download the APK below onto your Android phone.

Open the downloaded file. Android will ask whether to allow installs from your browser or Files app — allow it. This is the normal "install unknown apps" prompt for anything that doesn't come from the Play Store.
In the app's Settings, choose your provider (Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini), paste your API key, and pick a model.
Optional but recommended: enable TapLex under Android's Settings → Accessibility — it makes screen capture lighter on the battery.
Tap Start TapLex, open your game or manga, then tap the floating bubble and drag a box over the text you want to read.
apps.privacy: TapLex sends each captured image straight to whichever AI provider you choose, using the API key you enter — nothing is routed through this site or any server of mine. Your saved words and capture history live on your phone.
apps.buildNote: This is a developer (debug) build, shared as-is — the same app I use day to day, not a Play Store release. It installs by sideloading, which is why Android shows the extra permission prompts.
